era: Northern Netherlands (Drenthe), Neolithic, c. 3400 BCE, Funnelbeaker farmers.

sheets.subject: Northern Netherlands (Drenthe), Neolithic, c. 3400 BCE, Funnelbeaker farmers. Bright summer sky over flat land, a few broad cumulus clouds.
Northern Netherlands (Drenthe), Neolithic, c. 3400 BCE, Funnelbeaker farmers. Cool autumn sky with long low layered clouds and a few cumulus, wind coming.
Northern Netherlands (Drenthe), Neolithic, c. 3400 BCE, Funnelbeaker farmers. Flat open heathland with very gentle low rises, scattered distant birch clumps and juniper bushes.
Northern Netherlands (Drenthe), Neolithic, c. 3400 BCE, Funnelbeaker farmers. The distant edge of a dense wild deciduous forest of oak, lime and alder, an irregular treeline over flat land.

Northern Netherlands (Drenthe), Neolithic, c. 3400 BCE, Funnelbeaker farmers. Distant small cleared fields with tree stumps and low hedges, two tiny long wooden farmhouses with low thatched roofs, a thin line of wood smoke, forest edge behind.

Northern Netherlands (Drenthe), Neolithic, c. 3400 BCE, Funnelbeaker farmers. (1) a long hunebed (megalithic dolmen): two rows of large rounded glacial granite boulders carrying five huge rough capstones, low entrance on the long side; (2) a short hunebed with two capstones, partly covered by a low grassy earth mound.

Northern Netherlands (Drenthe), Neolithic, c. 3400 BCE, Funnelbeaker farmers. (1) a long farmhouse: wattle-and-daub walls between wooden posts, a thick thatched roof reaching low, a small doorway; (2) a small storage hut raised on four posts with a thatched roof; (3) a round wattle cattle pen.

Northern Netherlands (Drenthe), Neolithic, c. 3400 BCE, Funnelbeaker farmers. (1) a small patch of ripe emmer wheat with a few poppies at the edge; (2) a freshly cleared patch of ground with three tree stumps chopped by stone axes (rough cone-shaped splintered tops, never flat saw cuts) and a felled trunk with a chopped pointed end; (3) a stone-ringed fire pit with burning logs and a little smoke.

Northern Netherlands (Drenthe), Neolithic, c. 3400 BCE, Funnelbeaker farmers. (1) a broad old oak, (2) a slender silver birch, (3) a black alder. Each full figure from roots to crown top, side by side.
Northern Netherlands (Drenthe), Neolithic, c. 3400 BCE, Funnelbeaker farmers. (1) a young lime tree, (2) a gnarled hawthorn, (3) a Scots pine. Each full figure from roots to crown top, side by side.
Northern Netherlands (Drenthe), Neolithic, c. 3400 BCE, Funnelbeaker farmers. (1) a juniper bush, (2) a hazel shrub, (3) a low clump of heather, (4) a bramble patch.

Northern Netherlands (Drenthe), Neolithic, c. 3400 BCE, Funnelbeaker farmers. (1) a clump of tall common reeds, (2) a clump of tall wild grass, (3) a single large rounded glacial granite boulder, (4) a group of three smaller boulders.

Northern Netherlands (Drenthe), Neolithic, c. 3400 BCE, Funnelbeaker farmers. (1) a short straight section of woven wattle fence (hazel rods woven between upright stakes), (2) a short split-log post-and-rail fence, (3) a fallen dead tree trunk with broken branches lying on the ground.

Northern Netherlands (Drenthe), Neolithic, c. 3400 BCE, Funnelbeaker farmers. Prehistoric livestock, side view: (1) a small brown cow with short horns, (2) a calf, (3) a small sheep with dark brown primitive fleece, (4) a bristly dark pig.

Northern Netherlands (Drenthe), Neolithic, c. 3400 BCE, Funnelbeaker farmers. Arranged in two rows of three: (1) a Funnelbeaker clay pot with flared rim and vertical grooves, (2) a saddle quern (flat grinding stone with a rubbing stone on it), (3) a polished flint axe hafted in a wooden handle, (4) a wicker basket, (5) a wooden digging stick, (6) a stack of three clay bowls.

Northern Netherlands (Drenthe), Neolithic, c. 3400 BCE, Funnelbeaker farmers. Near foreground ground of a heath meadow: short grass with tufts, a few heather clumps, small stones and a worn footpath of bare sandy earth.

Northern Netherlands (Drenthe), Neolithic, c. 3400 BCE, Funnelbeaker farmers. Middle-distance band of open grassland and a small field of grain, with a low hedge of shrubs and a few young trees along it.

Northern Netherlands (Drenthe), Neolithic, c. 3400 BCE, Funnelbeaker (TRB) farmers. Arranged in one row of four, after real finds in the Drents Museum: (1) a Funnelbeaker clay pot (trechterbeker): round-bellied pot with a tall flaring funnel-shaped neck, rows of vertical incised grooves and small stab marks on the belly, hand-built, no handle; (2) a polished grey flint axe head fixed in a straight wooden haft, bound with no metal; (3) a single round amber bead with a hole through it, shown large; (4) a small group of five smooth rounded river pebbles.

Northern Netherlands (Drenthe), Neolithic, c. 3400 BCE, Funnelbeaker (TRB) farmers. Three separate set pieces: (1) a long low ramp of packed sand and turf sloping up from the ground to about two metres high, plain earth, nothing on it; (2) one huge rounded glacial granite boulder (a future capstone) lying on three peeled tree-trunk rollers on the ground; (3) a modern museum display case: a glass vitrine on a plain wooden plinth with one Funnelbeaker pot inside.

Two Neolithic farmhouses of the Netherlands drawn after archaeological reconstructions, side by side at the same scale, three-quarter view: (1) LEFT, a Funnelbeaker (TRB) farmhouse, c. 3400-2850 BCE, after the reconstruction at the Hunebedcentrum Borger: a rectangular house about 12 m long and 6 m wide, low walls of wattle-and-daub between upright posts, a gabled thatched roof of reed reaching low, one small doorway in the long side; (2) RIGHT, a Bandkeramiek (Linear Pottery) longhouse, c. 5000 BCE, after the excavated houses at Elsloo and Geleen in Limburg: a very long timber house about 30 m long and 6 m wide, walls of wattle-and-daub plastered with clay, a high steep gabled thatched roof, the long walls slightly bowed, a doorway at the short end.

Northern Netherlands (Drenthe), Neolithic, c. 3400 BCE, Funnelbeaker (TRB) farmers. Neolithic livestock, side view, same scale: (1) a small brown-grey goat with backward-curving horns and a short beard, (2) a small dark brown short-horned cow, smaller than modern cattle, (3) a small brown sheep with short wool and horns.

Northern Netherlands during the Saalian ice age, about 150,000 years ago: the edge of a vast flat ice sheet (land ice), a low white ice cliff running across the land with large granite boulders frozen into its foot and lying on the bare gravel plain in front of it, no trees, no people.
